transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi. Well, my regular doctor is the one who told me to come see you. He says I've gotten too thin. I mean, I can see what he means—my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me at my cleaning job lately. But, if I'm being honest, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and the number is lower.
Aside from feeling relieved when you see a lower number, do you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though others say you're thin?

Yes, I suppose I do. It's... well, if I eat something heavier, you know, like biscuits or a plate of pasta, I spend the rest of the day just scared that it's going to show on me. I end up checking myself in the mirror a lot, and I just can't stop thinking that I need to find a way to make up for eating it.
When you say you try to 'make up for' eating something like pasta, what exactly do you do—do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or exercise excessively afterward?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything like that. I'm on my feet a lot for work, cleaning and moving around, but I don't go out and exercise for hours on purpose. I just... I might skip my next meal, or I just try to eat a lot less the next day to balance it out.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how that compares to what you weighed before you started losing weight?

Well... I'm honestly not sure of the exact numbers. I haven't had my height measured in a long time, so I couldn't tell you that for sure. 

And with my weight, even though I check the scale, I don't really keep track of the exact number in my head. I just look to make sure it's going down. I don't really know exactly what I weighed before I started losing, either. I just know it's a lot less now than it used to be.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since you started losing weight?
Well, I'm 64, so... I haven't had a period in a long time. I went through menopause years ago, way before I started losing the weight. So, no, I haven't noticed any changes with that.
Do you happen to know roughly how much weight you've lost overall, in pounds or kilograms, since this started?

I really don't. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I just don't keep track of the actual numbers when I look at the scale. I know my work clothes are hanging off me a lot more than they used to, but... I couldn't give you an actual amount in pounds. I just haven't been paying attention to it that way.
About how long has this pattern of eating less and losing weight been going on—weeks, months, or longer?

Honestly, I'm not really sure. I haven't kept track of the time any more than the numbers on the scale. It's been... a little while, I suppose, but I couldn't tell you if it's been weeks or months. It just sort of started and... became what I do. I didn't mark it on a calendar or anything like that.
Would it be alright if we measured your height and weight right now, so we have an accurate current number to work with?
I suppose so. I mean, I don't really see the point, since I don't pay attention to the numbers anyway, but... if you need to, that's fine. We can do that.
Would you say that how you feel about yourself as a person—your self-worth—is closely tied to your weight or how your body looks?

Yes, I'd say it is. I mean... when I manage to stay small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right. Like I'm doing a good job keeping things together. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit full... I just feel like I've completely let myself go. It makes me feel like a failure, honestly. So, yes, how my body looks definitely changes how I feel about myself as a person.
Now that we've measured you, what are your current height and weight readings?

Well, you just took them... I don't really look at the scale, like I said. You wrote it down, didn't you? I think it was somewhere around five foot four, but I didn't catch the weight. You'd have the exact numbers on your chart there.
Based on your height and current weight that we just measured, do you know if your weight is still within a normal range for someone your height, or is it below what's considered normal?

Well... my regular doctor says I've gotten too thin, so I suppose it's below what's considered normal. I mean, I can see my work pants hanging loose on me while I'm doing my shifts, so I know I've lost. But... honestly, part of me still feels relieved when the number on the scale is lower.
